**D. glycolysis is activated at the onset of exercise.** When glycolysis speeds up, pyruvate is produced faster than the mitochondria can oxidize it, so more of it is converted to lactate. I'm changing my earlier answer, because a falling pH is a consequence of lactate and H⁺ accumulating, not a cause of more lactate production. The team note is wrong: lactate is made from pyruvate, so if pyruvate could not be formed, lactate production would stop (B is out), and readily available oxygen would lower lactate production (A is out).

CONFIDENCE: 72
